sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for slide drawing
sections.what: Brings in the helpers that set the slide's size, convert print points to screen pixels, set how text lines up vertically, and build addresses for images and files.
sections.why: Likely reason: the slide size and conversion rules are shared, so the drawing matches the shared template.
sections.watch_out: These helpers come from a shared template file, so changing them affects every place that draws slides.

sections.name: SlideScene (part 1)
sections.title: Fitting the slide to the screen
sections.what: Measures the width of the container and computes how much the fixed-size slide must shrink to fit. It watches for size changes and updates the scale when the window or panel resizes.
sections.why: The comment at the top says slides are drawn at true template size (1280 by 720) and scaled, so the preview matches the exported slide.
sections.watch_out: The scale starts at zero, so the slide stays hidden until the first measurement runs.

sections.name: SlideScene (part 2)
sections.title: Drawing the whole slide
sections.what: Draws every element on the slide at full design size and then shrinks the whole block to fit. Clicking the empty background clears the current selection when editing is turned on. Optional overrides let unsaved text appear as a live preview without being saved.
sections.why: The comment says this matches the backend PowerPoint writer, so the on-screen slide and the exported file look the same.
sections.watch_out: Fixed positions and the Arial font choice must stay aligned with the PowerPoint export, or the two outputs will differ.

sections.name: SceneElement (part 1)
sections.title: Drawing one shape or circle
sections.what: Draws a single rectangle or ellipse with its fill and optional border. In editing mode, an ellipse becomes clickable only when it is linked to a source, and a selected one gets a blue outline.
sections.why: Reason partly visible: only linked ellipses are clickable, which suggests they carry the data behind the chart point. Likely reason, not stated.
sections.watch_out: Clicking and keyboard selection are both wired up here, so changes to one must be checked against the other.

sections.name: SceneElement: if
sections.title: Drawing lines, images and text
sections.what: Draws lines as dashed or solid strokes, images from the template folder, and text boxes with font, size, alignment, color and bold or italic. Edited text overrides the stored text when a preview is active. One special element keeps its spacing exactly as written.
sections.why: Each element type needs its own drawing rule. The special case for one element id is kept for its title layout. Reason for that special case not stated.
sections.watch_out: An image element with no asset name draws nothing, so a missing image leaves a blank gap with no warning.

summary: Draws one slide on screen, placing its text, shapes and figures, so the editor and the thumbnail strip can show and click it.
purpose: Gives the slide editor and its thumbnail row a visual copy of each slide that the user can click.
why: Reason not stated in the code. Only the imports were included in this review.
how: Only the imports were provided, so the drawing steps are not confirmed. From how the editor calls this component, it receives a slide, optional unsaved text overrides, the selected element id, an interactive flag and a click callback, and it reports element clicks back to the editor.
inputs: A slide, optional unsaved text to show instead of saved text, the selected element id, a flag for interactive mode, and a click callback.
outputs: A drawn slide on screen, and a callback that tells the editor which element was clicked.
risks: Element sizes and positions come from the shared template helpers, so a change there changes this drawing too. Image addresses come from the scan API helper, so a wrong address shows a broken image.
debug: If slides look the wrong size or position, check the shared template file first, since this file only converts values. If images are missing, check the asset address helper and the server route it builds. If clicks do not select anything, check that interactive mode is turned on.
